chunks: Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Alā ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said:
If people knew the reward in the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), they would die of yearning and their souls would be torn apart with regret for it.
I asked, 'What is in it?' He said: 'Whoever goes to him with yearning, Allāh will record for him one thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand purified ‘Umrah.'
And the reward of one thousand martyrs from the martyrs of Badr, and the reward of one thousand fasting people, and the recompense of one thousand accepted charities.
And the recompense of freeing one thousand slaves seeking the Face of Allāh.
And he will remain protected for his year from every plague, the least evil of which is Shayṭān.
And an honourable angel will be assigned to him who will protect him from in front of him, from behind him, from his right, from his left, from above his head, and from beneath his feet.
So if he dies in that year, the angels of mercy will attend him.
They will attend his washing and shrouding, and seek forgiveness for him, and they will escort him to his grave while seeking forgiveness for him.
And space will be widened for him in his grave as far as his eye can see.
And Allāh will make him safe from the pressure of the grave and from Munkar and Nakīr so that they do not frighten him.
And a door will be opened for him to Paradise.
And his book will be given to him in his right hand.
And on the Day of Judgment, a light will be given to him which illuminates for his light from the East to the West.
And a caller will call out: 'This is the one who visited al-Ḥusayn with yearning for him.'
So no one will remain on the Day of Judgment except that he will wish on that day that he had been among the visitors of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him).

key_terms.كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ: His book (of deeds) in his right hand
key_terms.مُنْكَرٍ وَ نَكِيرٍ: Munkar and Nakīr (angels of the grave)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and blessings of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husain (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (a.s.), highlighting the eschatological magnitude of Ziyarat al-Husayn as a means of attaining divine protection and intercession. The narration emphasizes that the visitor’s yearning (tashawwun) transforms the act into a cumulative merit of thousands of good deeds, ensuring angelic guardianship and a distinguished status on the Day of Resurrection where all will envy such visitors.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh narrated to me from his father (‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā Al-Ash’ari), from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Alā ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)) said, “
If people knew the reward for going to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.), their souls would leave their bodies out of remorse and they would die yearning for it.”

I asked, “What is the reward for going to his Ziyārah?” Imam (a.s.) replied: Allāh will register the reward of one thousand accepted Hajj, one thousand purified ‘Umrah, one thousand martyrs from among the martyrs of (the Battle of) Badr, fasting of one thousand people, one thousand accepted SADAQAH, and the reward of freeing one thousand slaves in the way of Allāh for he who goes to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) yearning for him.
He will be protected for one year from every plague, the least evil of which is Shayťān.
And Allāh will dedicate an honourable angel to him who will protect him from the front, from behind, from the right side, from the left side, from over his head, and from under his feet.
If he dies in that year, the angels of mercy will attend (the rituals of) his ablution and shrouding and they will seek forgiveness for him.
They will also follow him in his funeral while seeking forgiveness for him.
His grave will be widened as far as he can see
and Allāh will keep him safe from the pressure of the grave and from being frightened by (angels) Munkar and Nakīr.
A door will also be opened from his grave to Paradise.
On the Day of Judgment, his book (of deeds) will be placed in his right hand
and he will shine with a light which illuminates everywhere from the east to the west.
(On that day), a caller will call out, “This is a person who went to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) yearning for him.”
Therefore, no one will remain on the Day of Judgment who will not wish he had gone to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.).
